studio.name: Audio Studio
studio.lead: Build sessions from your recordings and rhythm generators, preview them and export a multichannel WAV with a verification report. Sources are never altered.
studio.title: Title
studio.buses_hint: How many logical channels the project has. You choose the speaker layout at export.
studio.no_projects: Create a project, upload sources and place them on the buses.
studio.sources_lead: Uploaded files are stored unchanged: projects refer to them instead of copying. The SHA-256 checksum proves a file has not changed.
studio.no_sources: No sources yet. Upload a WAV, FLAC or AIFF file.
studio.upload_hint: WAV, FLAC or AIFF, 1 to 8 channels, up to 3 hours. Say where the material comes from and on what terms you use it.
studio.rights_source_hint: For example: “own voice recording, studio X”.
studio.rights_license_hint: For example: “all rights mine” or the licence name.
studio.place_hint: “Add” places the source on the {track} track at {at}.
studio.conflict: The project was changed in another tab or device. Your latest edits are not saved.
studio.device_downmix: The device has fewer than {n} outputs — the browser will downmix
studio.preview_fold_hint: Headphones 2.0 folds voice, music and back into stereo; pick the system profile to check channels exactly.
studio.inspector_empty: Select a clip on a track to edit it.
studio.gain_hint: 0 dB leaves the signal untouched, bit for bit.
studio.split_gen: Generators are not split: their phase starts at the clip start.
studio.generators_hint: A binaural generator is placed as a pair on neuro L and R: the frequency difference between the ears is the beat. An isochronic one goes on the selected track.
studio.ramp_order: The ramp must end after it starts, otherwise the project will not save.
studio.ramp_range: Values must be between {min} and {max} Hz.
studio.src_note: The {from} Hz source will be resampled to {to} Hz (SoX). The export report will say so.
studio.shortcuts_text: Space — play/stop · Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z — undo/redo · Delete — delete clip · S — split · + / − — zoom. Drag a clip to move it, drag its edges to trim.
studio.profile_drops: This profile has no buses for: {buses}. Their clips will not be in the file.
studio.allow_clip_hint: By default an overload is an error and no file is written. If allowed, the clipped samples are counted in the report.
studio.render_waits_save: Export becomes available once the project is saved.
studio.verified: passed: the file was read back independently; length, channels and SHA-256 match
studio.src_applied: Some sources were resampled — details in the report.
studio.router_lead: A custom profile decides which bus goes to which file channel and at what level, plus per-channel mute, polarity flip and delay (speaker alignment). Every save is a new version, so earlier exports keep their routing.
studio.router_empty: No custom profiles yet. The built-in ones are always available.
studio.router_layout_hint: The channel order is fixed by the WAV standard.
studio.router_caption: Matrix: rows are file channels, columns are buses, value is the level in dB
studio.router_cells_hint: Each cell is the bus level in that channel in dB: 0 is unchanged, −6 is half, up to +12. Empty means the bus is not sent there. Delay 0–100 ms.
studio.router_bad_gain: {ch} ← {bus}: the level must be a number in dB.
studio.fmt_hint: FLAC is checked by decoding it: the samples must match the WAV bit for bit.
studio.fmt_flac_float: FLAC cannot store 32-bit float — this project exports to WAV.
studio.lossless_ok: yes: the decoded FLAC matches the WAV bit for bit

err.too_many_channels: The source has more than 8 channels

studio.fmt_flac_wide: FLAC holds at most 8 channels, so a 7.1.4 layout exports as WAV.
studio.to_app_hp: A stereo export becomes the headphones track: the file is taken as it is, without processing it again.
studio.to_app_layout: The export becomes the {layout} version of the session made from this project: the file is taken as it is, without processing it again.
studio.to_app_sent: Sent. The track is being prepared on the app's Audio tab.
studio.to_app_no_apps: To send the export to the store, create an app first.

studio.all_started_app: The exports have started. When they are ready, the session is put together on the app's Audio tab.

carrier.name: Carrier
carrier.text: The generator’s main tone, the one you hear in the headphones. For a binaural beat the left and right channels get two carriers with a small difference in frequency.

beat.name: Binaural beat
beat.text: The difference between the left and right carrier frequencies: for example, 205 and 195 Hz give a 10 Hz beat. The file contains no sound at the beat frequency; the brain perceives it, so it has to be heard on headphones.

separation.name: Opposite carrier suppression
separation.text: How much weaker the other channel’s carrier is than the channel’s own: the left carrier in the right channel and vice versa. More dB means cleaner separation; for a binaural beat each ear should hear only its own carrier.

lufs.name: LUFS
lufs.text: A unit of perceived loudness (ITU-R BS.1770, EBU R128). Integrated loudness is the average over the whole track: −16 LUFS is louder than −23 LUFS. The converter measures it before and after; loudness changes only if the level had to be lowered because of a peak.

true_peak.name: True peak
true_peak.text: The signal’s peak level (in dBTP), including the values between samples that appear on playback. Above 0 dBTP some devices distort the sound, so the peak is kept below the ceiling.

gain.name: Common gain
gain.text: How many dB the converter changed the level of the whole track so the peak stays under the ceiling. 0 dB means the level was not changed. All channels change by the same amount, so the balance and the beat are kept.

dbfs.name: dBFS
dbfs.text: Level relative to the digital maximum: 0 dBFS is the loudest possible sample, −20 dBFS is ten times smaller in amplitude.

ramp.name: Ramp
ramp.text: How long the generator takes to rise smoothly from silence to the set level at the start of the clip and to fade the same way at the end, without clicks.

first.title: Where to start
first.lead: The way from an audio file to an app in the store. Every step can be saved and picked up later.
first.create: Create a draft: address, author, category and title.
first.audio: On the Audio tab pick a profile and upload a file. The conversion starts by itself.
first.qa: Check the quality report: listen to the result, look at the carriers, loudness and true peak.
first.program: On the Program tab build sessions from the finished tracks.
first.submit: Confirm the rights, set a price and send the version to moderation. Once approved, you publish it yourself or automatically.

lay.title: Versions for speakers and the chair
lay.lead: Each channel of the layout is a separate track. Any of them can take a file of its own, for example a voice in the centre. A channel without its own file is built from the main file. A finished version joins the session that plays the same main file by itself.
lay.need_file: Upload the main file in step 2 first.
lay.main_hint: The same file as the headphones track, so the versions match in length.

from_main.LFE: Low frequencies of the main file

lay.rules: The binaural difference plays only in the front channels. A channel's own file plays only in that channel and is mixed to mono if it is stereo. A file shorter than the main one ends in silence.
lay.listen_note: The file has {n} channels. On headphones and stereo speakers the browser mixes them down, so channel separation is heard only on equipment with enough outputs.
lay.check_ok: passed: shift only in the front, own files only in their channels
lay.studio_note: From the audio studio: “{project}”, snapshot {rev}, profile “{profile}”. The sound is taken as it is.

help.title: How to listen
help.how: How to listen and what you need
help.lead: What you need for headphones, speakers 3.0 and the NAP chair 5.1 and 7.1. The check below looks at your browser right now; nothing is sent to the server.
help.output_value: {n}, as set up in the system for the current output device
help.verdict: The {layout} version plays now. If you connect equipment with more channels, reload the page.
help.update_browser: This browser cannot play store tracks. Open the site in a current version of Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari.
help.hp_text: A binaural beat is heard only on headphones: each ear has to get its own channel.
help.hp_1: Any wired or wireless headphones and a current Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari will do.
help.hp_2: Before the session the player plays a tone on the left and on the right, so you can tell the channels are not swapped.
help.hp_3: Turn off mono audio and spatial audio in the system settings: they mix the channels.
help.multi_text: You need a computer output that carries separate channels. These work:
help.multi_1: HDMI to an AV receiver, TV or soundbar with multichannel PCM.
help.multi_2: A USB audio interface or USB receiver with 6 (5.1) or 8 (7.1) outputs.
help.multi_3: USB-C or DisplayPort through a monitor or dock with HDMI to the receiver.
help.multi_4: An optical output (S/PDIF) does not work: it carries only 2 uncompressed channels.
help.setup_1: Connect the receiver or audio interface and choose it as the output device in the system.
help.setup_2: Windows: Settings → System → Sound → More sound settings → the device → Configure → 5.1 or 7.1. macOS: Audio MIDI Setup → the device → Configure Speakers → Multichannel.
help.setup_3: Reload this page: the check above should show 6 or 8 channels. Then press Test speakers and make sure each channel plays from its own speaker.
help.setup_note: The browser sees as many channels as the system is set up for. If the device supports more but the check shows 2, change the speaker configuration.
help.offline_text: During the session the track is saved in the browser and checked against its checksum. Once the copy is ready, the session continues without a connection. In private mode the browser may not allow saving; then playback stops without a connection when the loaded part runs out.

beat.m_shift_hint: The whole uploaded track is frequency-shifted: the left channel lower, the right higher. Every sound of the track reaches the ears with the beat difference; no separate tones are added.
beat.m_shift_layer: From the track plus a carrier layer
beat.m_shift_layer_hint: As above, with two quiet tones of the same difference on top. The beat is more distinct, but the track gets a steady tone.
beat.m_layer_hint: The track stays as it is; the beat comes from two added tones. This is how the converter worked before.
beat.hz_hint: The left channel shifts by −{l} Hz, the right by +{r} Hz.
beat.layer_hint: From −60 to −12. Quieter is less noticeable.
beat.transition: Change the beat smoothly during the session
beat.summary_curve: The beat moves smoothly from {from} to {to} Hz over {min} min, then holds.
beat.summary_both: Made from the track, with a carrier layer on top.
beat.summary_layer: Made by two added tones; the track is not shifted.
beat.qa_shift_layer: from the track plus the carrier layer
beat.preview_need_file: Upload a file in step 2 — then you can listen to 20 seconds with these settings here before converting.
beat.preview_note: This is the start of the track processed with the current settings. Nothing is stored: change the settings and listen again. The beat is heard on headphones.
beat.quiet: The track is very quiet: peak {db} dBFS. A beat made from it will be faint. Raise the level in the mix or choose the carrier layer.

cal.title: Calibrate speakers and chair
cal.lead: Sit where you listen. Play noise in each channel and even out the levels so every channel sounds equally loud. Add delay to speakers that are closer than the others: 1 ms is about 34 cm. The calibration is saved for this device and applied every time you listen; the sound inside each channel is not changed.
